verdict.root_cause: cartservice alerted but is not the failing component. Its own spans are fast (0.1-0.6ms self time), its Redis calls are fast, its logs are error-free and continuous, and every one of the 32 recorded changes to it was paired with a revert leaving baseline state with a clean ~1.3h gap before onset. The unexplained time sits on the caller side of the frontend->cartservice hop: in 8 of 10 traces the frontend client span's self time exceeds the whole downstream cartservice server span, with 0.7-2.2ms gaps before the server span starts. Checkoutservice shows the same shape - orders still complete end to end, but per-order wall clock grew from ~20ms to ~0.65s spread across payment, email and queue steps rather than concentrated in one dependency. A broad, caller-side slowdown affecting many hops with no errors anywhere is most consistent with the frontend/client-side call path waiting - transport, connection-pool or queueing saturation - rather than any single downstream being slow. No resource series were ever retrieved, so the underlying exhaustion cannot be named.
verdict.reasoning: Traces localize added time to the client side of the frontend->cartservice hop and exonerate cartservice handler and cache [tr_1acc6074b03c]. cartservice logs confirm no errors, no restarts, no dependency failures, yet paired request intervals widen from milliseconds to ~0.5s over six hours [tr_bedabf035e1f]. checkoutservice shows the same diffuse latency growth with all dependencies still succeeding [tr_d64c9ae9d951]. The change record removes deploy, injected-delay and REDIS_ADDR misconfiguration as live causes because all were reverted before onset [tr_67bb549f6840]. Both metric dispatches returned no samples at all, so error rate and resource series are unmeasured [tr_27ccd8aed2d7, tr_15e8ff0c49e1] - which is why confidence is low.
open_questions: No resource metrics (CPU throttling, memory, connection pool, GC, restarts) were ever collected for frontend or cartservice, so client-side saturation is inferred, not measured.
Trace sampling covered 15:52-21:52, ending an hour before onset at 22:52:45; no traces from the incident window itself were examined.
checkoutservice logs were truncated to the oldest 8 and newest 32 lines, so error lines in the middle of the window remain unobserved.
frontend, loadgenerator and the other 8 services in the blast radius were never directly queried; the shippingservice->quoteservice hop flagged in one trace is also unexplored.

alternatives.root_cause: Gradual resource exhaustion in the frontend or shared node (connection pool, threads, CPU quota) is what makes the client-side waits grow over hours.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and mechanically compatible with the caller-side gap, but zero resource series were retrieved so nothing distinguishes it from transport latency; explicitly flagged as unsupported by measurement.

alternatives.root_cause: An unreverted residue of the traffic-shaping sidecar or REDIS_ADDR experiment cycles still perturbs the cart call path.
alternatives.why_not: The change record shows every mutation matched by a revert with no net drift, and the latency sits on the caller side of the hop rather than inside cartservice or its Redis calls.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric or log stream should follow from this proposal. The observable state should remain as recorded: cartservice server spans 0.4-2.2ms with 0.1-0.6ms self time, Redis child spans 0.2-1.1ms, cartservice logs continuous and error-free, checkoutservice PlaceOrder flows still completing with advancing queue offsets at ~0.65s per order. What should happen next is measurement, not remediation: retrieve container CPU throttling, memory working set, restart counts, GC pauses and connection-pool/gRPC channel saturation series for frontend and checkoutservice over 2026-09-17T16:00Z..23:00Z, and pull traces from inside the incident window (22:52:45 onward) rather than the 15:52-21:52 sample that ends an hour before onset.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the withheld resource series, once retrieved, name a specific saturating component with a matching change entry inside the incident window - for example a frontend config change altering pool size or timeouts, or a restart-count series on frontend climbing from 22:52:45. Either would convert an inferred client-side saturation into a measured one and could meet the preconditions for revert_config or restart_service. It is also wrong if the middle of the checkoutservice log window, currently unobserved due to truncation to oldest 8 / newest 32 lines, contains error lines that reclassify this as an error incident rather than a latency one. Note that the mechanism proposed by the verdict - caller-side transport or pool queueing - has no metric currently collected that could show it improving, so even a plausible action here would produce an effect nobody in this system could observe; that alone argues against acting.
proposal.risk: Acting anyway carries real cost. rollback_image and revert_config both fail their stated preconditions: the last image change was a revert ~1.9h before onset and the last REDIS_ADDR change a revert ~1.3h before onset, with a clean gap and every one of the 32 mutations paired to a revert, so there is no change inside the window to undo - reverting would push cartservice off its verified baseline and inject a new variable mid-incident. restart_service is irreversible and its precondition (evidence pointing at process state) is not met: cartservice logs show continuous serving with no restart banners, and no process-state series were ever collected for frontend. A restart of frontend would drop in-process cache and every in-flight request while orders are, per the logs, still completing - degrading a degraded-but-serving system into a briefly non-serving one, and destroying the very process state that would have diagnosed a pool or GC problem.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody, by construction - no service is touched and no caller sees a reset. For contrast, had an action been taken: restarting or redeploying frontend would be seen by loadgenerator and every user-facing path, and by its downstreams cartservice, adservice and recommendationservice as dropped connections; touching cartservice would be seen by frontend and checkoutservice. All twelve services in the blast radius remain in their current state under this proposal.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerting simultaneously along the cart/checkout/frontend path is a coherent user-facing failure, not a single quiet latency warning, so it cannot be dismissed despite the warning label. No open incidents to attribute it to, and nothing in the alert pattern points to a specific cause yet.
